name: Queen's Gambit
description: One of White's oldest and most powerful positional openings, offering a flank pawn to secure dominating central control.

variations.name: Queen's Gambit Declined (QGD)
variations.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O

explanations.d4: White controls the center with the queen's pawn.
explanations.d5: Black stakes a claim in the center.
explanations.c4: White offers the Queen's Gambit, fighting for central dominance.
explanations.e6: Black declines the gambit solidly, supporting d5.
explanations.Bg5: White pins the f6-knight to apply pressure.
explanations.Be7: Black breaks the pin and develops the bishop.
explanations.O-O: Black tucks the king away to safety.

variations.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted (QGA)
variations.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Bxc4 c5

explanations.dxc4: Black temporarily accepts the gambit pawn to ease development.
explanations.Nf3: White develops knight preventing immediate e5.
explanations.e3: White prepares to recapture the c4-pawn.
explanations.Bxc4: White recovers the gambit pawn actively.
explanations.c5: Black strikes back against White's center.

variations.name: Slav Defense
variations.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5

explanations.c6: Black plays the solid Slav Defense, protecting d5 without blocking the light-squared bishop.
explanations.a4: White prevents b5 and prepares to recover the pawn.
explanations.Bf5: Black develops the bishop safely outside the pawn chain.

variations.name: Semi-Slav Defense
variations.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 e6 5. e3 Nbd7

explanations.e6: Black transitions into the dynamic Semi-Slav Defense.

variations.name: Catalan Opening
variations.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 d5 4. Bg2 Be7 5. Nf3 O-O

explanations.g3: White prepares the powerful Catalan fianchetto setup.
explanations.Bg2: White places the bishop on the long diagonal.

variations.name: Grünfeld Defense
variations.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. e4 Nxc3 6. bxc3 Bg7

explanations.g6: Black prepares the hypermodern Grünfeld Defense.
explanations.e4: White builds a broad central pawn duo.
explanations.Nxc3: Black trades the knight to undermine White's center.
explanations.Bg7: Black fianchettos to put heavy pressure on White's center.

variations.name: Queen's Indian Defense
variations.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6 4. g3 Ba6 5. b3 Bb4+

explanations.b6: Black prepares to fianchetto the queen's bishop (Queen's Indian).

variations.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
variations.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e3 O-O 5. Bd3 d5

explanations.Bb4: Black plays the Nimzo-Indian, pinning the knight to control e4.

variations.name: King's Indian Defense
variations.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5

explanations.e5: Black strikes back against White's center to ignite kingside counterplay.

variations.name: Albin Countergambit
variations.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e5 3. dxe5 d4 4. Nf3 Nc6 5. a3 Bg4

explanations.e5: Black offers the sharp Albin Countergambit, fighting fiercely for initiative.
explanations.d4: Black pushes the pawn deep into White's territory to create tactical chaos.
explanations.Nc6: Black develops knight, increasing pressure on d4.
explanations.Bg4: Black pins the knight to target the d4 pawn controller.
